clue.text: Orphaned prophet to admit where he came from?

indicators.note: an orphan has lost a parent, so the prophet's name loses its MA, a familiar word for mother

parts.note: Mahomet is an old English spelling of the name of the Prophet Muhammad
to own something is to admit or confess it

explanation.surface: A prophet who lost his parents confesses where he grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orphaned' takes MA (mother) from MAHOMET, leaving HOMET. The surface also echoes the saying that a prophet is without honour in his own country.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's home town is the place they come from, where they were born and raised.

clue.text: P to show affection to men

parts.note: to hug is to embrace someone fondly
hes, plural of he, are males

explanation.surface: A poet wants to show fondness to men.
explanation.walkthrough: P is poet throughout: Ted Hughes, a Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Hughes was an English poet and Poet Laureate, husband of Sylvia Plath.

clue.text: P of little length and weight

parts.note: a mil is a thousandth of an inch, a tiny length
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A poet of small stature but great heft.
explanation.walkthrough: P is poet throughout: John Milton, author of Paradise Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the seventeenth-century English poet of Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Move convulsively to tease companion

parts.note: to twit is to tease or taunt
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Jerking about to wind up one's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a sudden involuntary jerk of a muscle.

clue.text: Linguistic items have value for P

parts.note: words are the items of a language
worth is value

explanation.surface: Words are precious to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: P is poet throughout: William Wordsworth, the Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet and Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Eggs in transmission?

definitions.meaning: a set of eggs laid and hatched together by a bird
the pedal-operated device in a car's transmission that engages and disengages the gears

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a brood of eggs and the coupling in a vehicle's drive train.

clue.text: Don't interfere with small boy being able to rise

parts.note: leave it means let it alone
Ned is a pet form of Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: Leave the little lad alone so he can get up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough that has been raised with yeast can rise, so it is described this way.

clue.text: Frighteningly bad?

parts.note: as a plain phrase means awful; read literally it describes something causing terror

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means very bad and, at root, causing terror.

clue.text: Manage to retain control

definitions.meaning: to keep a job is to manage to retain it
to restrain or keep under control

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to keep a job and to restrain someone.

clue.text: Old dance where girl, untruthful one, died

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
someone who tells untruths is a liar
D is the usual abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tale of a dishonest girl who perished at an old-time dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The galliard was a lively sixteenth-century court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Comic award for six of the Ps?

definitions.meaning: Stan ..., the thin half of the comedy double act ... and Hardy

definitions.text: award for six of the Ps?
definitions.meaning: the ... wreath is the poet's honour, and six poets in this grid (Dryden, Wordsworth, Tennyson, Betjeman, Hughes, Motion) were Poets Laureate

explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel was a famous film comedian, and a laurel crown symbolises honour bestowed on poets.

clue.text: I aim to correct bad spelling

definitions.text: I aim to correct bad spelling

parts.words: I aim to correct bad spelling
parts.note: reads like a pedantic proofreader, but the bad spell is a demonic possession that this person drives out

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who casts out evil spirits works to undo a malign spell, which is bad spelling in a punning sense.

clue.text: Ancient P rewriting his ode

indicators.note: rewriting the words his ode signals that their letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An old poet revising one of his odes.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle P stands for poet throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesiod was an early Greek poet, author of Works and Days, so an ancient poet.

clue.text: Spread of gas grieves belligerent

indicators.note: a spread means the letters of gas grieves are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: The spread of gas upsets someone combative.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent and combative are synonyms for hostile, ready to attack.

clue.text: P, six-footer, lying down?

definitions.meaning: in this puzzle P stands for a poet: here Henry Wadsworth ..., the American poet
a tall man stretched out flat is literally a ...

explanation.definitionFit: The American poet of Hiawatha bears this surname, and a tall man lying down is a long chap.

clue.text: P to put shirt on man's head when embraced by girl

parts.note: to put one's shirt on is to bet everything

indicators.note: the girl's name wraps round the following letter

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A poet gambles everything on a man who is hugged by a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes M from man's, and 'when embraced by' puts it inside JEAN. P is poet throughout: John Betjeman, Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Betjeman was a much-loved English poet and Poet Laureate.

clue.text: The French church deprived of its leader in Ireland

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: the church word loses its first letter

parts.note: a minster is a large church

explanation.surface: A French church losing its head, oddly sited in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of its leader' removes M from MINSTER. The definition is the place: a province in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four provinces of Ireland, containing Dublin.

clue.text: Please, if you would, cook goose, do, after breakfast starts

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the first letter
the start of the word breakfast is its first letter
to cook something is to alter it, so goose do is rearranged

explanation.surface: A polite request to cook the goose once breakfast is begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like an instruction to the reader in the polite surface, but it is the anagram signal; 'after' places the rearranged letters behind the opening letter of breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Be so good is a polite formula meaning please, kindly do this.

clue.text: Simple yet real complex about people

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the people
complex here means intricate or tangled, so the letters of yet real are mixed up

parts.note: men is a common crossword synonym for people

explanation.surface: Something simple can still be real yet complicated where people are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges YET REAL into ELETARY, and 'about' puts it round MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or simple, as in Holmes's elementary deductions.

clue.text: P with bird at home

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
in means at home

explanation.surface: A poet with a songbird indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: P is poet throughout: Philip Larkin.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was the English poet of The Whitsun Weddings.

clue.text: Exam for students if in Alsace- Lorraine,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Exam for students if in Alsace- Lorraine,' ends in a comma, apparently cut short; FINALS is hidden in 'if in Alsace' but no hidden indicator survives other than 'in', which is part of the run
annotationWithheld.clue: Exam for students if in Alsace- Lorraine,

clue.text: Uninteresting study of P

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A dull study of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: P is poet throughout: John Dryden, Restoration Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the Restoration poet and first official Poet Laureate.

clue.text: P sounds like the writer of their lives

indicators.note: signals that the name of the writer is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Samuel Johnson wrote Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets, so he wrote poets' lives

explanation.surface: A poet whose name echoes the biographer of the poets.
explanation.walkthrough: P is poet throughout: Ben Jonson, the Jacobean poet and playwright, sounds like Samuel Johnson, author of Lives of the Poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson was a celebrated English poet and dramatist, a contemporary of Shakespeare.

clue.text: In which training bears fruit?

parts.note: sounds like praise for education paying off, but describes a frame on which trees are trained flat against a wall and crop

explanation.definitionFit: A trellis or lattice on which fruit trees are trained flat; its trained trees literally bear fruit.

clue.text: Proposal for P

definitions.meaning: a formal proposal put to a meeting for debate
in this puzzle P stands for a poet

explanation.definitionFit: A formal suggestion debated at a meeting shares its name with Andrew Motion, the poet.

clue.text: Patience was required for three quarters of a mile with a little less help

indicators.note: taking three of the four letters of the word mile, from the front

parts.note: a kilometre is a distance a little less than a mile, abbreviated km
aid means help

explanation.surface: Patience was needed to cover most of a mile, with ever less assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is the title heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera, a village dairymaid. 'three quarters of' takes MIL from MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience in the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta is a dairy girl, an example of this occupation.

clue.text: P from Chile set Auden right

indicators.note: set here means arranged, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A Chilean poet takes Auden's measure correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Neruda was the Nobel-winning Chilean poet.

clue.text: P for game heard being played?

indicators.note: heard signals that the name of the game is taken by its sound

parts.note: tennis is a racket game
a match that is on is under way

explanation.surface: A poet named after a game one hears in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: P is poet throughout: Alfred Tennyson, the Victorian Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate who wrote In Memoriam.
